q: Your embedding model accepts at most 512 tokens. Some chunks are 900 tokens long. What happens to them?
o: The model splits them into two vectors automatically
The text after the limit is truncated, so that part never influences the vector
The index rejects the table
Nothing: longer chunks always give better vectors
e: Inputs beyond the maximum length are cut off. Keep every chunk below the embedding model's limit, measured in tokens.

q: A vector index has grown too large for its endpoint. Which change reduces the number of chunks?
o: Increase the overlap from 10% to 30%
Switch from triggered to continuous sync
Use larger chunks or less overlap
Add more metadata columns
e: Overlap repeats text, so more overlap means more chunks. Larger chunks and less overlap mean fewer vectors.

q: You must index scanned paper contracts stored as PDF images. Which step is essential?
o: OCR, because the files contain images of text and no text layer
`beautifulsoup4` to parse the PDF
Fixed-size chunking with no overlap
Enabling Change Data Feed on the volume
e: A scanned PDF holds pictures of pages. A plain text extractor finds nothing; an OCR tool or a layout-aware parser such as `ai_parse_document` is needed.

q: Why prepend the document title to a chunk before embedding it (a context-enriched chunk)?
o: It makes the chunk shorter
It is required by Delta Sync indexes
It removes the need for a primary key
A chunk such as "If the router password changed..." does not name its product; the title adds that context to the vector
e: Chunks cut from the middle of a document lose the context of the whole. Adding the title or section helps the vector, and the retriever, know what the chunk is about.

q: What is the best way to choose between fixed-size and sentence chunking for your documents?
o: Always use the smallest possible chunks
Build both, run the same retrieval evaluation set, and compare metrics such as top-k accuracy
Pick whichever produces the most chunks
Use the default of your library; chunking does not affect answers
e: Chunk size, overlap and strategy behave like hyperparameters. Measure them with labelled questions and the documents that should be retrieved.
